title: 'Lonely' Brain Waves in Sleep Linked to Weaker Memory
paragraphs: During deep sleep, the brain makes slow waves. In healthy young people, these waves travel across the brain. Scientists think they help the brain keep new memories.

Researchers at the University of California, Berkeley studied young adults and older adults. Older people had waves that travelled a shorter way. The scientists call them 'lonely waves'. Brain scans showed that people with more tau protein in the front of the brain had more lonely waves.

In the evening, people learned pairs of words. The next day, people with more lonely waves remembered fewer pairs. These people did not have Alzheimer's disease. The scientists say the results show a link, but they cannot say that tau causes memory problems.

questions.q: What do the scientists call the short waves?
What did people learn in the evening?
Can the scientists say tau causes memory problems?
questions.a: No, they only see a link.
